Worksheet 1 | HL Focus

Course Enrolment Reporting

This worksheet is only about the HL aggregate content. Use the prepared course enrolment dataset to write grouped queries with COUNT, AVG, SUM, MAX, MIN, GROUP BY, and HAVING.

COUNT AVG SUM MAX MIN HAVING
Open HL Dataset All HL SQL worksheets

Dataset

  • 4 linked tables with 36 enrollment rows
  • Enough data for grouped summaries by department, course, level, and semester
  • Designed for reporting queries rather than basic retrieval practice

HL Focus

  • A3.3.4 aggregate functions on grouped data
  • Reporting and decision-making from summarized results
  • Choosing the right grouping column and threshold

Before You Start

  • Assume the SL query skills are already secure.
  • Focus on what each group represents before writing the SQL.
  • Remember: WHERE filters rows and HAVING filters groups.
1

Count the Groups

Start with row counts so you can see how the data is distributed.

Reference pattern — COUNT and GROUP BY 
-- Count rows in each group
SELECT group_column, COUNT(*) AS row_count
FROM table_name
GROUP BY group_column;

-- Count after a join
SELECT category_column, COUNT(*) AS row_count
FROM first_table AS a
JOIN second_table AS b
    ON a.primary_key = b.foreign_key
GROUP BY category_column
ORDER BY row_count DESC;

GROUP BY creates one summary row per group. COUNT(*) tells you how many source rows ended up in each summary.

  1. A3.3.4 COUNT

    Count how many courses each department offers.

  2. A3.3.4 COUNT

    Count how many enrollment rows each course has.

  3. A3.3.4 COUNT

    Count how many enrollment rows fall in each semester.

2

Average, Total, Highest, and Lowest

Move from raw counts into richer summary measures.

Reference pattern — AVG, SUM, MAX, MIN 
-- Average a numeric value in each group
SELECT group_column, AVG(number_column) AS average_value
FROM table_name
GROUP BY group_column;

-- Add up a numeric value in each group
SELECT group_column, SUM(number_column) AS total_value
FROM table_name
GROUP BY group_column;

-- Find the largest and smallest value in each group
SELECT group_column,
       MAX(number_column) AS highest_value,
       MIN(number_column) AS lowest_value
FROM table_name
GROUP BY group_column;

Aggregate functions collapse many rows into one summary. Choose the grouping column first, then decide which measure helps answer the reporting question.

  1. A3.3.4 AVG

    Calculate the average score for each department.

  2. A3.3.4 AVG

    Calculate the average score for each course.

  3. A3.3.4 SUM

    Sum the course credits by level so you end up with one total for SL and one total for HL.

  4. A3.3.4 MAX / MIN

    Return the maximum and minimum score in each course.

3

Filter Groups with HAVING

Now add thresholds to the grouped results.

Reference pattern — HAVING after aggregation 
-- Keep only the groups that meet a threshold
SELECT group_column, COUNT(*) AS row_count
FROM table_name
GROUP BY group_column
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 4;

-- HAVING can also test averages or totals
SELECT group_column, AVG(score_column) AS average_score
FROM table_name
GROUP BY group_column
HAVING AVG(score_column) > 85
ORDER BY average_score DESC;

HAVING is for group-level conditions. If the condition is about the summary, it belongs after GROUP BY, not in WHERE.

  1. A3.3.4 HAVING

    Show only departments with at least 9 enrollment rows.

  2. A3.3.4 HAVING

    Return only courses whose average score is above 85.

  3. A3.3.4 Report query

    Produce a department report showing department name, enrollment count, and rounded average score, ordered from highest average to lowest.

  4. A3.3.4 Decision-making

    Write one sentence explaining how a head of department could use your final report to support a planning decision.

Model Answers — Course Enrolment Reporting

Section 1

1
Example count query 
SELECT d.DepartmentName, COUNT(*) AS CourseCount
FROM COURSE AS c
JOIN DEPARTMENT AS d
    ON c.DepartmentID = d.DepartmentID
GROUP BY d.DepartmentName
ORDER BY d.DepartmentName;

Section 2

2
Average and total examples 
SELECT d.DepartmentName, ROUND(AVG(e.Score), 1) AS AverageScore
FROM ENROLLMENT AS e
JOIN COURSE AS c
    ON e.CourseID = c.CourseID
JOIN DEPARTMENT AS d
    ON c.DepartmentID = d.DepartmentID
GROUP BY d.DepartmentName;

SELECT Level, SUM(Credits) AS TotalCredits
FROM COURSE
GROUP BY Level;

Section 3

3
HAVING example 
SELECT d.DepartmentName, COUNT(*) AS EnrollmentCount
FROM ENROLLMENT AS e
JOIN COURSE AS c
    ON e.CourseID = c.CourseID
JOIN DEPARTMENT AS d
    ON c.DepartmentID = d.DepartmentID
GROUP BY d.DepartmentName
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 9
ORDER BY EnrollmentCount DESC;
